title: Customer reports an authorised payment impersonation scam
case_summary: The customer reports receiving a call from someone claiming to be from the bank's fraud team. The caller said the account was at risk and instructed the customer to move money to a new account described as safe.
customer_statement: The customer says they believed they were speaking to the bank and authorised the payments following the caller's instructions. This account has not been independently corroborated.

chronology.event: Customer reports receiving a call from a person claiming to be from the bank.
chronology.source: Customer account; call record not yet reviewed

chronology.event: Customer says caller warned that funds were at risk and instructed a transfer to a safe account.
First payment authenticated by the customer.
Second payment authenticated by the customer.
Third payment authenticated by the customer.
Customer contacts the bank to report suspected scam.

recorded_facts.text: Three outgoing payments totalling AUD 19,000 are listed in the supplied transaction data.
The supplied service record shows the customer contacted the bank at 13:15.

customer_statements.text: The customer says the caller claimed to represent the bank and instructed transfers to a safe account.
The customer says they personally authorised the payments because they believed the caller.
customer_statements.verification_status: Authentication records supplied; circumstances require review

observations: The customer-reported call and instruction precede the three payments in the supplied chronology.
The payments were made to two newly described beneficiary accounts.
The supplied material does not establish who controlled the beneficiary accounts or what happened to the funds afterwards.
unknowns: Origin and identity of the caller.
Whether the call can be linked to any known impersonation activity.
Beneficiary account ownership and any onward movement of funds.
Whether any funds were held, recalled or recovered.
Whether device, authentication or contact records provide additional relevant evidence.
next_enquiries: Preserve and review available call, digital channel and authentication records under bank procedures.
Establish beneficiary account details and examine available onward movement information.
Record the timing and outcome of relevant recall, hold or recovery enquiries.
Assess the customer's account of events alongside available independent records.
provisional_position: Suspected impersonation scam reported by the customer. Further enquiries are required to establish the caller, beneficiary links and fund movement. The bank's authorised fraud process determines the outcome.
quality_notes: The chronology and payments are supplied, but the caller, beneficiary control, onward movement and recovery outcomes remain unresolved.
